data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Astringent solution (aluminium subacetate/acetate, usually diluted 1:20–1:40)

## Mechanism of action
- Aluminium salts precipitate proteins → astringent (shrinks and dries weeping skin), mildly antibacterial; evaporation cools

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Wet compresses for acute weeping eczema, contact dermatitis (poison ivy), pompholyx, infected eczema, otitis externa
- Soaks for bullous and erosive lesions

## Dose & formulations
- Dilute 1:20 to 1:40; apply compresses for 15–20 min 2–4 times daily for 2–3 days

## Adverse effects
- Over-drying with prolonged use; irritation

## Contraindications
- Prolonged use on dry skin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Wet compress for weeping dermatitis — 'if it's wet, dry it'

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Burow's solution — aluminium subacetate solution). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
